subject: MSA & Order Form — quiet-period and brand-acknowledgment redlines
messages:
From: Carla Ruiz <carla.ruiz@prospectco.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: ProspectCo Legal <legal@prospectco.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form — quiet-period language & brand acknowledgment

Connor —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is the MSA/Order Form redline from our legal team (ProspectCo_MSA_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx). We flagged two items we need to resolve to keep the deal on schedule:

1) "Quiet period" / announcement timing: we proposed a 30-day quiet period following public launch for any joint press or case studies.
2) Brand acknowledgment & logo use: we added a clause requiring written approval of any public-facing copy and a short one-paragraph testimonial pre-approval.

Can you confirm Redwood's comfort with those points or propose alternative language? We need a sign-off by the end of next week to meet our procurement timeline.

Attachments:
- ProspectCo_MSA_OrderForm_v2_redline.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Thanks,
Carla Ruiz
Head of Legal Operations
ProspectCo
carla.ruiz@prospectco.com
(415) 555-0182
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Carla Ruiz <carla.ruiz@prospectco.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T10:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — quiet-period language & brand acknowledgment

Carla —

Appreciate the redline. Looping in Priya (account lead) and Evelyn (legal) so we can get an internal view on the semantics and approval flow. A couple quick asks from my side:

- Is the 30-day quiet period tied to our marketing/public release date or customer-first-public-announcement? We want to be aligned on the trigger.
- On the brand copy approval, can you clarify whether "written approval" needs to be legal sign-off or product marketing sign-off? That affects speed.

Evelyn/Priya — please review the attached redline and chime in with proposed changes.

I can be flexible on timing if we can get a clear approval path.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive — Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
(650) 555-0123
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Carla Ruiz <carla.ruiz@prospectco.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — quiet-period language & brand acknowledgment

Carla / team —

Thanks for sending — I reviewed with Evelyn and Karthik. High-level proposed changes we put together (please see our attached redline RFQ_Redline_ConnorProspect_v1.docx):

- Quiet period: propose a compromise of a 14-day quiet period tied to the first public announcement date, not the internal launch. This keeps momentum for joint comms while giving both teams time to prep.
- Brand acknowledgments: allow a one-paragraph customer quote and logo use for case studies and landing pages, subject to "pre-approval not to be unreasonably withheld" within 5 business days.
- Logo usage: request a small technical appendix limiting logo modifications and specifying proper trademark attribution.
- Confidentiality carve-out: add a narrow carve-out that permits Redwood to reference the customer in non-sales internal reporting.

If ProspectCo prefers a longer quiet period, what would be the business reason? That will help us evaluate risk and escalate if needed. Our timeline: we need final language by 2027-05-25 to hit the onboarding milestone.

Attachments:
- RFQ_Redline_ConnorProspect_v1.docx (redline summary)

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
From: Carla Ruiz <carla.ruiz@prospectco.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — quiet-period language & brand acknowledgment

Priya / team —

Thanks for the suggested edits and the quick turnaround. I reviewed with our procurement lead and we can be flexible — but we have an internal comms blackout policy that typically prefers a 21-day window for joint press around strategic integrations. The asks are:

- Can Redwood accept 21 days instead of 14? It gives our comms team time for approvals across regions.
- For the "pre-approval within 5 business days" language, please specify the approval owner (example: "Customer's marketing director or legal may approve"). It helps avoid back-and-forth.

Quoted for context:
> On Tue, May 18, 2027 at 10:01 AM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:
> 
> Appreciate the redline. Looping in Priya (account lead) and Evelyn (legal) so we can get an internal view on the semantics and approval flow.

We can accept the logo usage language as proposed provided the approval owner is named. If that works, I can push procurement to sign the Order Form the same week.

Carla Ruiz
Head of Legal Operations
ProspectCo
carla.ruiz@prospectco.com
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Carla Ruiz <carla.ruiz@prospectco.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-20T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form — quiet-period language & brand acknowledgment

Carla —

Appreciate the context and the flexibility. Redwood can accept a 21-day quiet period tied to the public announcement date. For approvals, we'll add the following language: "Customer's marketing director or designated communications lead shall have 5 business days to approve marketing collateral; if no response is provided within that window, approval will be deemed granted unless reasonable objections are raised in writing."

Approval flow we will follow:
- Redwood creates draft copy and logo usage mockups (Product Marketing).
- Customer marketing director (named approver) reviews within 5 business days.
- If customer raises objections, Redwood resolves or escalates to legal for final sign-off.

I've attached an updated Order Form that incorporates the agreed language: OrderForm_ProspectCo_Connor_v4.docx. If that looks good, can you confirm procurement will sign once legal has done a final pass? Also let us know if you want a short addendum to the NDA to reflect the quiet-period exception (we can prepare one).

Attachments:
- OrderForm_ProspectCo_Connor_v4.docx (proposed final)

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive — Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference
